newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse split plan to boost industrial.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse split plan to boost industrial.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp's modified plan to separate its media and industrial businesses will give the industrial group positive cash flow and leave it debt free, company officials said Wednesday.
"That's a dramatic change from our original plan," Kevin Ramundo, vice president of corporate communications, said in a conference call with reporters.
Under the original plan, the industrial operations would have had to absorb $375 million in annual costs to pay for pension benefits, he said.
The company announced today it was altering its orginal plan by keeping Thermo King, a refrigerated transport unit, with the media company, to be called CBS Corp.
The original plan called for Thermo King to be grouped with Westinghouse's other industrial operations: Power Generation, Energy Systems and Government and Environmental Services.
Westinghouse also planned to spin off up to 20 percent of Thermo King after the separation and use the proceeds for the other industrial units, which have not been as profitable.
Ramundo said Westinghouse will consider a reverse stock split for the industrial group after the separation, to enhance its market value.
Analysts have predicted the industrial group, to be called Westinghouse Electric Co, will trade in a range of $3 to $4 per share after the separation.
In a news release, Westinghouse said it will consider options to enhance Thermo King's value to shareholders, including a sale, public offering or spin-off to shareholders.
It said the new plan will not affect the timing of the separation, scheduled to be completed in the third quarter.

"The modified plan, which reflects the numerous unsolicited inquiries that have been received for Thermo King, is more beneficial to shareholders than the plan we announced last November," Westinghouse Chairman Michael Jordan said in a news release. "By retaining Thermo King, we have greater flexibility to apply its strong cash flow to reduce liabilities and also to maintain several attractive options to optimize its value."
Westinghouse said the industrial side benefits because the cash savings from retaining pension obligations at CBS outweighs the lost cash flow from Thermo King.
